title: Control-plane HTTP client does not honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY

verdict.rationale: The evidence shows the transport code was copied verbatim from entiredb and later had its timeouts tuned. Nothing in it mentions proxy behaviour or chooses to leave `Proxy` unset, so the missing proxy support looks like an oversight rather than a decision. No prior ruling covers this behaviour.

rulings.text: Ruling on issue #2160 (Feature request: Goose and Qwen Code agent integrations): we don't add agent integrations to the CLI directly. New agents go through the external agent path first, standalone entire-agent-<name> binaries in https://github.com/entireio/external-agents that talk to the CLI over the external agent protocol. Once an integration is well tested and broadly used, we can consider pulling it into the CLI source tree. Closing as not planned for the CLI itself. [source: gtrrz-victor (CONTRIBUTOR), 2026-08-31, https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2160#issuecomment-5476033646]

entiredb and into the CLI so a single binary can serve both roles:
when invoked as `git-remote-entire` (via a shipped symlink), `main()`

stream.

    fuzzer in this repo).
  - replaced entire.io/version.GitRemoteHelperAgent() with a

    `git clone entire://` for the current login.

ok, let's do the proper thing

Loosen connect timeouts for slow links

Bump the default per-host TCP connect timeout 2s -> 4s (satellite links
saw no node respond under 2s on push), and give the cold replica-discovery
probe its own more patient 10s budget — that first "which nodes serve this
repo" contact pays a cold DNS+TLS handshake to a possibly-distant entry LB
and has no failover to fall back on, so a tight budget fails the whole
clone/fetch. Replica failover keeps the short default so dead nodes are
still skipped quickly.

An explicit ENTIRE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS now overrides every connect
timeout (discovery included) via os.LookupEnv, instead of being floored.

git-remote-entire's auth client (cluster /.well-known discovery + token
exchange) also uses the patient discovery budget: it talks to single
control-plane hosts with no failover.

[assistant] rall HTTP timeout. The initial cold request to the entry domain (DNS + TLS to a possibly distant region/LB) intermittently takes >2s to connect, which trips it.

- **`internal/entireclient/httpclient/transport.go:24`** — `DefaultDialTimeout = 2 * time.Second`. This is the per-host connect budget, used by the transport that `git-remote-entire` builds (`cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:107`).
- The 30s value the broader search surfaced is the whole-request `http.Client.Timeout` — not what's flaking.

## The catch

## Summary of this round

**1. Env override now applies to all connect timeouts (`os.LookupEnv`)** — `internal/entireclient/httpclient/transport.go`
- New `envConnectTimeout()` helper uses `os.LookupEnv`. When `ENTIRE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is set to a positive int, both `DialTimeout()` and `DiscoveryDialTimeout()` return that exact value — no flooring. Unset/blank/invalid falls back to each function's own default.

**2. Default dial timeout 2s → 4s** — for your satellite-internet push problem.
- `DefaultDialTimeout = 4 * time.Second`. `DefaultDiscoveryDialTimeout` stays 10
